name: core--docker-daemon-nofile
description: Raises the ops host's Docker default file-descriptor limit from 1024 to 64000 via /etc/docker/daemon.json, and bundles live-restore so that this is the last daemon restart that stops containers. Docker's 1024 default is below MongoDB's required 64000, and below it mongod does not degrade — it throws TooManyFilesOpen from a noexcept path and terminate() kills it with SIGSEGV, which presents as memory corruption and was misdiagnosed four times in imotbgScraper2026's test suite.

implementation.change: New task file imported from tasks/main.yaml under tag docker_daemon, plus docker_daemon_config / docker_daemon_min_nofile / docker_daemon_restart in defaults/main.yaml. The config is rendered from a dict with to_nice_json and installed with a JSON validate hook, because dockerd refuses to START on a malformed daemon.json — which on this host means every container down with no obvious cause. The restart is gated behind docker_daemon_restart (default false), the same shape as caddy_enabled and imot2026_enabled: it stops the Caddy public edge, RocketChat, LiteLLM, the AI stack and music-production-engine, so it is an explicit decision with a chosen moment. When the flag is off the play prints what is still pending rather than silently leaving inert config.

checks: MEASURED: a fresh container reported ulimit -n of 1024 before the change

MEASURED: default-ulimits is NOT applied by SIGHUP — daemon.json written, `systemctl reload docker` issued, a fresh container still reported 1024 (Docker 29.2.0). This is why the task restarts rather than reloads
MEASURED: after the daemon restart a fresh container reports 64000, and `docker info` reports LiveRestoreEnabled=true — so this was the last daemon restart that stops containers
MEASURED: all 21 containers came back; chat.koeff.com answered 200 and musicengine.koeff.com 303 afterwards
MEASURED: the imot2026 stack was then deployed onto the raised default and its mongod has not segfaulted since — the failure that motivated this change

KNOWN LIMIT: a restart applies the new default only to containers created afterwards. mpe-mongo and rc-mongo were recreated by the restart and so did pick it up; any container started before it and never recreated would not have.
